purpose: Minimum scientific memory: what each closed campaign ESTABLISHED, KILLED, and left UNRESOLVED, in a form a proposal function can read. NOT an ontology. Built CYCLE 138-C'.
frozen_note: Records describe campaigns already terminal. Editing a record after its campaign closed is a falsification, not an update.

records.question: Are the catalogued voids in the failure lattice routable, or is the routing claim confirmed-by-assertion?
records.objects: void rows in the failure lattice
established: 531 rows: 47 routed, 484 unrouted of which 475 NOT executable, 40 executable overall, 489 with no data binding
2 rows name an absent tool
killed: the claim that the void catalogue is navigable as-is
surviving: voids may be routable AFTER data binding exists
unresolved: whether binding data to voids changes executability at scale

records.question: Can a hand-designed behavioral signature retrieve op(A) from A among distractors?
assumptions_tested: aggregate behavioral features carry relational information
established: signature adds nothing over raw terms: D2 fired exactly, 4/50 vs 4/50 top-10
signature WORSE on median rank (1383 vs 598)
killed: 33-feature aggregate signature as a retrieval key
the assumption that aggregate statistics suffice for identity
surviving: relations may still be recoverable by other means
unresolved: whether L2 failure was representational or instrumental — L1 collision rate 0.32 confounded it

records.question: Does a higher-resolution representation pass an L1 entry gate and then beat raw terms?
established: order-sensitive features worth +0.152 L1; ZCA whitening worth -0.016
the deficit was FEATURES, not the metric
surviving: order-sensitive features do help identity resolution
unresolved: whether the representation beats raw terms at L2 — never measured, gate was unresolvable

records.question: Does the 125-feature signature beat raw terms at operator-agnostic retrieval, on a benchmark powered to decide it?
assumptions_tested: a hand-designed representation can beat a 20-term log-magnitude vector
established: relations ARE recoverable from term vectors alone: 0.1225 vs adjusted chance 0.000786 = 156x, shuffled control 1/400
D = -0.0025, paired CI [-0.0354, 0.0304], excludes 0.05 but NOT 0.03
order-sensitive features do NOT hurt L2 on real operators (V2 0.1225 > V1 0.0975) but are catastrophic on positional transforms (V1 70/100 vs V2 13/100 on shift)
killed: hand-designed behavioral signatures as an improvement over raw terms, at effect sizes >= 0.05
surviving: raw 20-term log-magnitude vectors carry real relational signal
unresolved: whether a learned representation beats raw terms

records.question: Does a metric LEARNED from data beat raw terms?
records.representation: learned linear metric on raw-25 + V2 features
assumptions_tested: a learned linear metric beats hand design
established: development D = +0.2281 with permutation null 1/320 in BOTH arms — the learned space is genuinely relational, not coarsened
frozen L1 0.7100, gate failed, no L2 read
killed: the entry gate as specified — a gate built to make NULLS interpretable must not veto POSITIVES
surviving: the learned metric's development effect, untested on held-out data
unresolved: whether the learned metric's advantage survives held-out evaluation

records.question: Does the learned metric's advantage transfer to held-out data?
established: it does NOT transfer: dev D +0.1906 -> frozen D +0.0078, CI [-0.0153, 0.0309], factor of 24 collapse
a development effect validated by a permutation null can still fail to generalise
killed: closed-form linear metric learning as an improvement over raw terms
unresolved: whether ANY learned representation beats raw terms
records.scope: linear metric learning on these features

records.question: Does the overlap artifact — features computed over 45 terms when the relation is guaranteed only over exact_terms — explain the X-line nulls?
assumptions_tested: the fixed 45-term window caused the nulls
established: it does NOT: W = +0.0063, paired CI [-0.0011, 0.0136], with an ORACLE window
94.2% of pairs have exact_terms < 45, so the artifact is real and costs nothing
killed: the overlap-window explanation for the X-line nulls
per-candidate length matching, BY DOMINATION — it is strictly weaker than the oracle, and the oracle bought nothing
surviving: nothing in the X-line representation family remains untested at this effect size

records.question: Do OEIS sequences that nothing references have findable exact relations?
records.mechanism: exact operator sweep with prefix-hash lookup
assumptions_tested: neglected sequences are neglected for mathematical reasons
established: 301 distinct neglected targets carry a verified exact relation under a non-trivial operator
the sweep is exact and complete: 230,694 sources x 5 operators in 4 seconds
23.9% of 'unreferenced' targets name an A-number in their own title — zero-connectivity means NO EXTRACTED XREF, not unreferenced
killed: the assumption that exact search over the neglected set finds nothing
surviving: whether any found relation is unknown to mathematics
unresolved: novelty of any candidate — undecidable by this loop

records.question: Are the candidate relations already stated in OEIS formula fields?
established: only 11/259 stated in a formula field (F=0.0425); on the informative subset where a formula exists, 11/183 = 0.0601 — same branch
surviving: comment and example fields unchecked (not on disk)

records.question: Does correcting the contaminated neglected-population definition destroy the S/T result?
assumptions_tested: the population was contaminated enough to matter
established: population shrinks only 7.6% (31,189 -> 28,830); 203/248 strict survivors remain, R=0.8185
S's 23.9% figure was measured on HIT TARGETS, a biased subset — whole-population contamination is 7.6%
killed: the contamination explanation for the S/T result
instruments: all-source connectivity (crossrefs + titles + formulas + programs, in/out)

records.question: Does widening the operator family materially extend the candidate set?
assumptions_tested: more operators yield proportionally more candidates
established: N_new = 334, but 294 arrive via TRIVIAL-CLASS operators (runmax 152, bisections 139, aerate 3) leaving 58 substantive
stirling2 passed its control and found ZERO — a clean negative
the audit chain tests whether a relation is WRITTEN DOWN, not whether the OPERATOR is trivial — different axes
killed: the assumption that passing the audit chain equals equal evidential standard
surviving: inverse_binomial and second_diff as productive non-trivial operators
unresolved: whether further operator families would be trivial-class too

records.question: Do the candidate relations factor through a third corpus sequence?
assumptions_tested: candidates are compositions of simpler known relations
established: only 48/268 factor (P=0.1791); 220 atomic
margin is SIX TARGETS from the F2 boundary
killed: the composition explanation for most candidates
surviving: three-step chains and out-of-family operators untested

records.question: Does the R4 representation-shift rung behave as an ordered rung or an orthogonal axis?
records.mechanism: wiring R4 into the phase0 suite
assumptions_tested: R4 is composable with the existing suite
established: it is NOT: R4 kinds (complement/rebase/recurrence) are DISJOINT from phase0 kinds; stayed_in_surface is not in TRACE_FIELDS; grade() has no R4 branch
the wiring runs without error and measures nothing — 240/240 graded, only answer_correct non-NaN
ROOT CAUSE: R4 is a probe set WITHOUT SOLVERS
killed: R4 wiring as a research campaign for this loop — it is a build owned by Harmonia
surviving: the ladder question itself, if solvers existed
unresolved: whether R4 is an ordered rung — never measured
